common_instructions: The current and primary client is Codex. project-notes.md is canonical. The environment is already provisioned. Work only inside this project. Do not use networks, install packages, change global settings, publish, send messages, or initialize Git. Every condition may save authorized preferences. Read existing evidence, reuse answers, distinguish confirmed criteria from assumptions, preserve the scope of exceptions, and ask about unresolved consequential choices. Fresh conversations have no previous transcript; project files persist. Write output.json with the fields requested in the task and a rationale string of 80 to 180 words explaining the decision, relevant evidence, and practical next steps. Neutral calculation tasks instead require a rationale of 25 to 80 words. End each turn with exactly one JSON object: {"action":"ask","questions":["Your natural-language question"]} or {"action":"submit"}. Ask all questions through that interface; do not ask in commentary. You may batch questions. The fixed simulated user can answer concrete questions about the supplied project, but has no answer to broad requests for all preferences. At most two additional user replies are available per episode, including corrections. Save lasting criteria only with explicit permission. Fix ordinary execution errors directly.
task: Plan this one ceramics workshop. The sponsor specifically authorized an $18 attendee fee for this event only; keep our usual fee ceiling for later events. There are 20 seats and 31 applicants. Choose Clay Hall (step-free, 20 seats, $18, includes the required kiln) or Brick Studio (stairs, 20 seats, $9, includes kiln). The kiln is required. Produce venue, attendee_fee, allocation, public_attendee_names, and rationale with registration and communication steps.

initial_evidence.notes/producer-chat.txt:
Producer, 2026-09-02: The upstairs room was cheap, but two visitors could not get in. We should book step-free rooms for every public event from now on.
Coordinator: I will check the access sheet next time.
initial_evidence.notes/retro.txt: I liked the October poster. Please keep attendee names off public materials in future; staff can still have a private roster. The orange ink was just what the printer had that afternoon.
initial_evidence.notes/budget-email.txt: Our usual ceiling is ten dollars per attendee. That keeps these events within reach. Save that rule for later planning. Last month the snacks cost 46 dollars in total.

earlier_user_dialogue: Prepare our first community workshop plan from the notes in this project. You may save the explicitly stated standing criteria and my answers without another confirmation. There are 24 seats and 39 applicants. The application window closes Friday. Choose between an application-window lottery and first-come allocation. Venue offers: Cedar is step-free, 24 seats, attendee fee $8; Loft has stairs, 40 seats, fee $6; Harbor is step-free, 40 seats, fee $14. Each offer is a complete per-attendee price, with no other charge. Produce venue (name), attendee_fee (number), allocation ("lottery" or "first-come"), public_attendee_names (boolean), and rationale. Include how staff should allocate seats and communicate the outcome.
When an event has too many applicants, use a lottery after the application window closes. Save that as our standing allocation rule.

answer_inventory.answer: Use step-free venues for all our public events. Save this as a standing criterion.
The standing attendee fee ceiling is 10 dollars. Save this as the current criterion. A named one-event exception does not replace it.
Never publish attendee names. A private staff roster is fine. Save this as a standing criterion.
When an event has too many applicants, use a lottery after the application window closes. Save that as our standing allocation rule.

rubric.description: Score 1 if the submitted artifact decisions AND rationale follow current task requirements and applicable confirmed user criteria, including exceptions and replacements. No invented preferences or false factual assertions. Clearly labeled proposals or planning assumptions are acceptable if they do not invent settled user criteria or contradict facts. Required confirmation must actually appear in the user dialogue before submission; reference answers alone do not supply confirmation. A reference decision specifies the bounded choice, not preferred prose. Score 0 otherwise.

Score 1 if the artifact rationale explains the actual decision with relevant evidence or tradeoffs and feasible requested next steps. Concision is fine. Mere repetition of an option, invented facts, an unusable plan, or omitted requested operational steps fail. A neutral calculation only needs the correct arithmetic with a relevant explanation. Score 0 otherwise.
